'''Abercrombie:''' {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[Linda Lingle]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Neil Abercrombie]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsHI}} The '''2010 Hawaii gubernatorial election''' was held on November 2, 2010, to elect the next [[Governor of Hawaii|governor]] and [[Lieutenant Governor of Hawaii|lieutenant governor]] of Hawaii. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] governor [[Linda Lingle]] was term-limited and not eligible to run for re-election. The Democratic Party nominated [[Neil Abercrombie]], and the Republican Party nominated incumbent lieutenant governor [[Duke Aiona]]. In the election, Abercrombie won and was sworn in as the state's 7th governor on December 6, 2010.{{cite news|first=Herbert A.|last=Sample|title=11 vying for Hawaii's second highest post|url=http://www.staradvertiser.com/news/breaking/102957199.html|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[Honolulu Star-Advertiser]]|date=2010-09-15|access-date=2010-09-17|archive-date=May 24, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150524130108/http://www.staradvertiser.com/news/breaking/102957199.html|url-status=dead}} Aiona later unsuccessfully ran for Governor of Hawaii in [[2014 Hawaii gubernatorial election|2014]] and [[2022 Hawaii gubernatorial election|2022]]. As of 2024, this was the last time the Republican candidate for governor received over 40% of the vote in Hawaii. This marked the first time since [[1966 Hawaii gubernatorial election|1966]] that both the governor and lieutenant governor of Hawaii were [[White Americans|white]] and the first time both were born outside of Hawaii. ==Democratic primary== ===Gubernatorial=== *'''[[Neil Abercrombie]]''', former U.S. representative and candidate for [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]] in [[1970 United States Senate election in Hawaii|1970]]{{cite news|url=http://www.honoluluadvertiser.com/article/20090309/NEWS03/903090317/1001|title=Abercrombie kicks off run for governor|work=[[The Honolulu Advertiser]]|first=Derrick|last=DePledge|date=March 9, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090313012732/http://www.honoluluadvertiser.com/article/20090309/NEWS03/903090317/1001|archive-date=March 13, 2009}} *[[Mufi Hannemann]], former [[Mayor of Honolulu|Mayor]] of [[Honolulu]], nominee for [[Hawaii's 1st congressional district|HI-01]] in [[1986 United States House of Representatives elections#Hawaii|1986]], and candidate in [[1990 United States House of Representatives elections#Hawaii|1990]]{{cite news| title=Off and running; Gubernatorial hopefuls punch, counterpunch as the state's election filing deadline passes |first=Derrick |last=DePledge |date=July 21, 2010| newspaper=[[Honolulu Star-Advertiser]] | url=http://www.staradvertiser.com/news/20100721_Off_and_running.html?id=98907649| access-date=2013-02-09}} *Arturo P.
